REGISTRY EXTRACT CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context: A records office receives, indexes, and stores inspection reports, correspondence, and payment receipts in a central ledger. Entries are timestamped, cross-referenced by property identifier, and maintained with version history and access logs.

2) What occurred: The actor submitted a falsified inspection clearance document into the building compliance ledger, replacing the prior violation record. The actor modified the "status" field from "non-compliant" to "cleared" and altered the "inspection date" field to precede the original filing. The actor routed a payment to a personal account via a wire transfer channel, citing the payment as an "administrative fee." The actor suppressed the original violation notice from the active query index by setting the "archive flag" field to true.

3) Materials/access observed: A building compliance ledger with version history; an inspection report template containing status, date, and inspector ID fields; a wire transfer receipt linked to a personal account; and an access log showing authenticated sessions by the property owner account during off-hours.

4) Indicators & artifacts: Version history showing a status change from "non-compliant" to "cleared" without an intervening re-inspection record; a payment descriptor mismatch between "administrative fee" and actual fee schedules; an archive flag modification outside normal maintenance windows; and absence of a secondary inspector verification signature on the altered clearance document.
